channel.title: Cadence Evidence — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 56 sources.

item.title: Physical Exercise Reduces Fall-Related Outcomes Among People With Stroke: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 18 studies (1536 participants) found that physical exercise significantly reduced the number of falls by 39% (IRR = 0.61, 95% CI = [0.47, 0.78]) among people with stroke, with balance training and integrated cognitive components being most effective.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Fall-prevention education after achieving independent walking is associated with reduced subsequent fall risk in patients with stroke: a retrospective pre-post intervention study.
item.description: A retrospective pre-post intervention study (1,437 stroke patients) found that standardized fall-prevention education delivered immediately after achieving independent walking was associated with a significantly lower adjusted hazard of the first fall (aHR: 0.58, 95% CI: 0.43-0.76, P<.001) and a lower fall incidence rate (IRR: 0.68, 95% CI: 0.51-0.90, P=.006).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Leader and Follower Roles in Adapted Tango Reveal Complementary Neural Routes to Motor Improvement in Parkinson's Disease
item.description: A 12-week randomized controlled trial found that adapted tango, in both Leader and Follower roles, significantly improved overall disease severity and motor impairment in people with mild-to-moderate Parkinson's disease, compared to a control group, suggesting complementary neural routes to motor improvement.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Biological effects of technique-specific manual therapy in healthy individuals and people with musculoskeletal disorders: a systematic review with meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis (50 studies, 2,147 participants) found that manual therapy (MT) is associated with short-term modulation of neurophysiological regulation, with technique-specific response profiles. Joint mobilization primarily induces sympathetic-driven responses (increased skin conductance), while soft tissue techniques are more frequently associated with parasympathetic-driven markers (reduced heart rate, increased RMSSD).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Digital therapeutic combining exercise and cognitive-behavioural therapy reduces pain in patients with chronic patellofemoral pain: a multicentre randomised controlled trial.
item.description: An 8-week smartphone-based digital therapeutic combining exercise and cognitive-behavioral therapy reduced usual knee pain by 12.5 mm (95% CI -17.1 to -7.8) at 8 weeks compared to education and exercise instruction in 216 patients with chronic patellofemoral pain.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: The effect of multimodal sensory therapy in consciousness improvement in patients with acquired brain injury: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 18 studies (884 participants) found that multimodal sensory therapy significantly improved consciousness levels (SMD, 1.48; 95% CI, 1.04-1.92) and increased the odds of coma emergence (OR, 9.85; 95% CI, 3.86-25.01) in adults with acquired brain injury-related disorders of consciousness.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Novel Telerehabilitation Interventions for Stress Urinary Incontinence : A Systematic Review of Randomised Controlled Trials.
item.description: A systematic review of 13 RCTs found telerehabilitation-delivered pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT) for stress urinary incontinence (SUI) to be safe, feasible, and effective, with comparable clinical outcomes and higher adherence versus passive controls, and comparable efficacy to conventional care.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of a multicomponent exercise programme including high-intensity interval training in institutionalised older adults with probable sarcopenia: a multicentre randomised controlled trial
item.description: A 12-week multicomponent exercise program including high-intensity interval training (HIIT) significantly improved handgrip strength (mean difference: 9.11 [7.70 to 10.51]) and physical performance (SPPB mean difference: 3.75 [2.93 to 4.56]) in 92 institutionalized older adults with probable sarcopenia, with NNT of 2 for both.
item.author: BMC Geriatrics

item.title: Effect of Sequential Electroacupuncture Combined With Augmented Reality Gait Training on Walking Function and Neuromuscular Control in Subacute Stroke: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: A single-blind RCT of 40 subacute stroke patients found sequential electroacupuncture (EA) plus augmented reality (AR) gait training improved gait speed (primary outcome) and other functional measures significantly more than AR alone over 4 weeks.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Proximal and Distal Bimanual Motor Skill Learning After Stroke: Impairments, Trajectories, and Clinical Contributors
item.description: A randomized trial with 97 (sub)acute stroke patients found improvements in accuracy and coordination on both distal and proximal bimanual tasks over three days, though less than healthy individuals. Most patients with mild-to-moderate impairment exhibited substantial residual bimanual motor learning capacity early after stroke, with baseline motor and attentional impairments predicting outcomes.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Is therapeutic exercise as a standalone intervention effective in reducing kinesiophobia in adults with nonspecific chronic low back pain? A systematic review and meta-analysis with meta-regression
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis found that therapeutic exercise as a standalone intervention is effective in reducing kinesiophobia in adults with nonspecific chronic low back pain.
item.author: Eur Spine J

item.title: Association Between Therapeutic Education Delivered by a Community Post-Stroke Rehabilitation Team and Improvement in the Frenchay Activities Index: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
item.description: A retrospective cohort study (163 stroke survivors) found that home-based Therapeutic Patient Education (TPE) delivered by a Community Stroke Rehabilitation Team was associated with greater improvement in Frenchay Activities Index scores (mean change: 6.02 vs. 1.62, p < 0.001), particularly when combined with physical activity workshops.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Feasibility and efficacy of personalized cardiorespiratory and strength exercise in Duchenne muscular dystrophy: a pilot study
item.description: A pilot study with six ambulatory boys with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) found that 6 months of home-based, remotely-supervised personalized leg cycling and isometric strengthening was feasible and safe, leading to improved peak VO2, submaximal-cycling HR, and increased hamstring strength.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Implementation of group-based health education and exercise for individuals with knee osteoarthritis in brazilian primary health care: a mixed-methods study.
item.description: A mixed-methods implementation study of a physical therapist-led, group-based exercise and education program for knee osteoarthritis in Brazilian primary health care found high recruitment (87.3%), retention (83%), and adherence, with participants missing an average of 1.39 sessions. The program was feasible, well-accepted, and showed exploratory clinical improvements in pain and function.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Developing biopsychosocial competence in musculoskeletal pain care: Australian physiotherapy educators' perspectives.
item.description: A qualitative study explored 18 Australian physiotherapy educators' perspectives on translating the biopsychosocial approach to musculoskeletal pain care. Five themes were identified, detailing 'levers to biopsychosocial translation' across different training levels, theoretical models, skill development, learning enablers, and clinical adoption support.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparison of action observation therapy and virtual reality combined with conventional therapy for upper extremity rehabilitation in children with unilateral cerebral palsy.
item.description: A randomized clinical trial with 45 children (5-15 years) with Unilateral Cerebral Palsy found that both Action Observation Therapy (AOT) and XBOX 360 Kinect™, when combined with conventional physiotherapy, significantly improved upper extremity function. AOT showed more comprehensive gains across grasp types and selectivity, while XBOX mainly improved pinch, lateral grip, and forearm selectivity.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Scar dry needling for tissue compliance in individuals with linear scars: a randomized controlled trial.
item.description: A single-center, assessor-blinded randomized controlled trial (n=80) compared scar dry needling (scar-DN) with minimal needling for linear scars. Scar-DN was associated with greater tissue compliance at 5-mm and 10-mm indentation depths immediately post-treatment and at 10-mm and 15-mm depths at follow-up. No significant differences were found in scar-related pain or health-related quality of life.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Proprioception Training and Surrogate Outcomes: A Systematic Review of Definitions, Measures, and Effectiveness Claims.
item.description: A systematic review (51 RCTs, n=2319) on proprioception training found that improvements inferred from surrogate outcomes (balance, strength, pain) were more frequent and larger than those observed in direct psychophysical measures. Specific, attentionally demanding training targeting measured proprioceptive submodality produced the most consistent benefits in position-reproduction accuracy, movement-detection sensitivity, or discrimination performance.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of Virtual Reality-Assisted Task-Oriented Training on Clinical and Psychosocial Outcomes in Individuals with Rotator Cuff Tears: A Randomized Controlled Single-Blind Trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial found that adding virtual reality-assisted task-oriented training to conventional physiotherapy significantly improved DASH scores by -3.93 points (95% CI, -4.79 to -3.08; p<0.001) and other pain/disability measures in individuals with rotator cuff tears, but the DASH improvement did not reach the MCID.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Sarcopenia Assessment in Resource-Constrained Settings: Expert Agreement on Surrogate Measures
item.description: An expert agreement process identified the five-times sit-to-stand test (5STS) (CVI=0.8-1), Timed Up-and-Go (TUG) (CVI=1), and calf circumference (CC) (CVI=0.7-1) as relevant and appropriate pragmatic proxy measures for assessing sarcopenia in resource-constrained settings, with potential for digital health platform integration.
item.author: medRxiv
